title: Steer Fabric: Latency-Aware Geographic Hedging and Capacity Hints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Requests across regions sometimes experience tail latency spikes or silent capacity saturation that cause downstream SLO violations. Existing region selection is either strict geo-pin (good for locality) or coarse latency hedging that ignores per-node capacity signals. Goal: design and implement a "steer fabric" controller that makes per-request routing decisions using (1) latency budgets, (2) soft geo-pinning with jittered affinity, and (3) lightweight capacity hints including token-bucket headroom and short-term load estimates. The controller must integrate with circuit-breakers and load-shedding policies so that failing regions are automatically deprioritized or shed without causing global avalanche. Deliver a runtime-ready implementation with metrics, a canary rollout, and runbook integrations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New steering controller returns routes for 99% of requests within 250us median decision time in production canary traffic.
2) For a synthetic cross-region latency spike test, client-side P99 across canary routes does not exceed baseline P99 + 20% while global SLO remains satisfied.

3) When a region reports >80% token-bucket utilization and increasing queue depth, the controller reduces routed traffic to that region by >=50% within 30s and falls back gracefully to other regions or model-variants.
4) Circuit-breaker integration: opens fast-path to skip saturated regions, with automatic rejoin after hysteresis window; documented in runbook.

5) End-to-end observability: per-request routing reason, scoring breakdown (latency_score, capacity_score, geo_affinity_score), and a dashboard with heatmap and rollback button are live in Console for canary workspace.
6) Config surface: operators can adjust latency_budget_ms, geo_favor_fraction, capacity_thresholds, and per-customer hard pins via API and Console.
7) No customer-facing error rate increase during 48-hour canary (<=1% relative increase).
design_decisions: A. Hybrid scoring: compute a weighted score = w_lat*lat_norm + w_cap*cap_norm + w_geo*geo_bonus; expose weights as runtime flags and dynamic config.
B. Soft geo-pinning: prefer same-region if score within delta, otherwise allow hedging to lower-latency region; tie-breaker includes fractional jitter to avoid synchronized failover.
C. Capacity hints: regions expose a 1s rolling token-bucket utilization ratio and a short queue-depth estimate. These are coarse to avoid control-plane pressure and accepted as best-effort signals.
D. Circuit-breaker coupling: when token-bucket or health-checks trip a CB, mark region as DEPRIORITIZED and inject a decay multiplier that increases shedding aggressiveness with severity.
E. Fast path: for premium customers with hard pins, allow override of steering but still subject to capacity_hard_limit to protect fabric.
F. Observability: attach route_decision metadata to traces (route_id, reason_codes) and emit aggregate metrics (route_fallback_count, route_shift_latency_impact).
G. Backwards compatibility: controller exposes a compatibility mode to emulate legacy geo-pin behavior for migrations.
H. Safety: add a global throttling circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation during rolling restarts.
I. Runtime placement: implement controller as a sidecar-like component in the edge request director to keep decision latency sub-ms and allow local cache of recent region hints.
J. Simulation-first: prior to rollout run a 72h simulator using production traffic traces with injected failures to validate hysteresis and jitter parameters.
implementation_notes: 1) New service code in repo: infra/steerbox-controller. Initial prototype as feature-flag behind /steer/v2 endpoint.
2) API contract: RouteDecision {region, model_variant, reason_codes[], decider_version}. Add route metadata header X-Steer-Reason.
3) Capacity hint ingestion uses a gRPC stream from region agents publishing every 500ms with aggregation at the director; fall back to health-check probes if stream unavailable.
4) Circuit-breaker behavior implemented via token-bucket + exponential backoff reopen policy; use existing cb library used by admission controllers.
5) Config stored in Consul/KV and surfaced in Console with a validation schema and safe defaults.
6) Ensure idempotent decision for retries: attach route_id to request so retry coordinator can keep affinity if desired.
7) Add unit tests for scoring math, and integration tests against local region simulators.
test_plan: - Unit tests for scoring and tie-breaking logic (edge cases: equal scores, stale capacity hints).
- Integration tests: loopback against two-region simulator with synthetic queues and latency jitter.
- Chaos tests: simulate region full-saturation and network partition to validate graceful degradation and no global error amplification.
- Performance: benchmark decision latency under 10k reqs/s with cached hints. Target median <250us and 99th <2ms.
- Canary: route 2% of real traffic from staging workspace for 48 hours; monitor SLOs and rollback on anomaly.
rollout_and_monitoring: - Stage 1: internal test cluster, run simulator runs, validate metrics and traces.
- Stage 2: canary to non-critical customer workspace (2%) for 48 hours. Alert if route_fallback_count increases >3x or p99 latency regresses >20%.
- Stage 3: 10% gradual ramp with automated rollback window and manual guardrails. Use Console rollback UI to revert weights or disable steer/v2.
- Runbook snippets: how to interpret 'DEPRIORITIZED' reason_code, how to nudge geo_favor_fraction, and steps to re-enable a region after capacity recovery.
- On-call escalation: if canary sees >5% error increase or repeated oscillation, page Reliability team and Schedule a postmortem within 48 hours.
